searchText: https://github.com/torquem-ch/verklecpp here is the repository, give me some time, and I will ping anyone interested once done Is there any IPA library for C++ out there? I have been searching it for a while and I cannot find it as of now Not that I'm aware of, I'd be surprised if there were okay then writting a verkle library in C++ is unfeasible for now I will take it up again perhaps in the future I am not a cryptographer, I think i will focus on integrating it in Erigon You can create FFI bindings if you want from either rust or go. I think thats what nethermind did but for the verkle trie layer does not makes much sense for Silkworm, if it has to be a precompile, why not use rust bindings for the entire structure it makes sense if it is completely in C++ but precompiles are nasty, better having one at a higher level than one at a lower one Ah right, yeah I think that implementing the crypto is a big undertaking, since the curve being used will unlikely be available in C++ yeah, i underestimated the task, the technology is more novel than merkle trees There is much more complexity involved to implement them from scratch I may pick it up again in the future, but for now let's make the repository private Yeah its quite complex, I have a document above that details all of the methods needed by the trie layer from the cryptography layer, for when you do decide to pick it up again You can for the most part, just mock those methods and implement the trie logic in the meantime, I will integrate them in Erigon yeah that i saw, but then it would not work so let's see what the silkworm team decides Yeah it would only work for ensuring that the trie logic is correct, you will need to implement the cryptography later on to make sure it is interopable. Its mostly just a strategy to separate the two layers Cancun is the name of the fork that enables verkle trees. It's the one after Shanghai and Paris <@353136597522448385> just a clarifications, are the keys and values of KeyValuePair always a 32 bytes hash or the value can sometimes be 0?
